game: NYG@WAS Week 5 2026 (kickoff/venue not in pack; spread/total not saved)

script.base: No spread or total is saved, so this is a form script, not a market script. Washington blitzes 47% and NYG dropback EPA is -0.55 vs blitz (+0.29 when not blitzed), so Winston's efficiency is capped and the NYG engine is Cam Skattebo (50 carries, 154 yards in weeks 2-4) with Isaiah Likely as the target leader (27 targets). Washington is without Stefon Diggs (22 targets / 115 yards / 197 air yards over those three weeks) and Terry McLaurin is questionable, so WAS leans on Jayden Daniels' scrambles plus a Jacory Croskey-Merritt / Rachaad White committee against an NYG run defense that has allowed 4.88 YPC and 11 runs of 10+. Base case is competitive and messy, run-and-checkdown, not a shootout.
script.flip1: The blitz gets home, WAS scores first and leads late. NYG abandons the run, so Skattebo's carry total stalls while pass attempts rise into negative EPA; WAS clocks it with Croskey-Merritt, which can revive JCM's faded rush line (last four rush yards 63, 43, 36, 15) and only helps White if he is not the one sitting.
script.flip2: NYG hits explosives on unblitzed plays against WAS safeties Nick Cross, Percy Butler and Tyler Owens, all out. Nabers (195 air yards L3), Malachi Fields (205 air) and Likely (181 air) yardage comes in, WAS trails, the WAS run game is abandoned, and Daniels' scramble line (7 carries, 69 yards L3) is the rusher that lives.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and this lost because the backfield roles did not hold. Washington trailed after NYG explosives against Cross, Butler and Owens, never gave White the 4-5 carries that 20.5 needs, and Croskey-Merritt, Allen or a returning McNichols soaked what rushes there were. On the other side Skattebo was a pure runner — 50 carries already say that is his job — and the blitz answers went to Likely and Nabers, so he posted another 0- or 8-yard receiving line while the 13.5 looked soft on paper. A full McLaurin plus a WAS lead would have been the other miss, clocking JCM and starving both the White carry and, if NYG never had to throw, the Skattebo target. Unresolved questionable tags are enough to keep both at a lean and to refuse a sized slip.
slip_story: One story only: a competitive, blitz-heavy, run-capable game. White rush over is the WAS answer to a soft NYG run defense with Diggs out; Skattebo rec over is the NYG answer to a 47% blitz. They fit the base script together and each survives a different flip, but a true WAS blowout or a true NYG shootout breaks one of them, so this is not a 3-4 leg build. Do not add Likely or Nabers overs (they need the unblitzed explosive flip), do not add a total (none saved), and do not add Croskey-Merritt over (opposite of the committee trend). No TDs, one market per player.
